title: Conditional transfer of supported finite-model comparison from integral to rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps, also for $\Omega$. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restriction $H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0'=T,$$
where each arrow is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J_k=(a_k)_!$ in the open case and $J_k=(a_k)_*$ in the closed case, and put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ for $r=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The symbol $T_0'$ is only the root of this chain; the closed member of the pair is $T_0$.
For any coefficient ring $R$ mentioned below, its sheaf is $R_V=p_V^*C(-,R)$; a finite scalar local model means a module locally isomorphic to $R_V\otimes_{\underline{R}}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $R$-module $P$, on a pro-étale cover. Define $\mathsf B_R(t)$ to mean: for every finite chain of the specified open and closed immersions ending in $T$, and every finite scalar local model $L$ on its source, the actual ordinary module-derived restriction
$$\rho_{R,J,L}:R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},J L[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*J L[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. This notation is just the displayed quantified property, not an additional definition node. It includes all chains, including the identity chain, with no quasi-compactness assumption on the complement of $t$.
Let $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$, or let $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $K=E$. Assume the additional comparison property $\mathsf B_R(t)$. Then $\mathsf B_K(t)$ holds. Here $K$ carries its norm topology and its full continuous-function condensed ring. The conclusion concerns all finite scalar local models over $K$, without supplying a global $R$-lattice for them; their transition maps may be arbitrary actual maps. The implication is for the fixed closed pair but for every admissible support chain. It does not assert comparison for images, kernels or quotients of such maps, or an equivalence of completed and uncompleted categories. The torsion cohomological-rigidity hypothesis on the pair is retained. No regularity or Noetherianity, invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes, or global integral-model hypothesis is added.

proof.text: Choose a coefficient map a and a finite extension-product presentation of every rational supported model using supported_rational_lattice_generation. This packages exactly the original stratified lattice, support projection and tree-reconstruction steps, without a cohomological hypothesis.

Let P(M) mean that the actual closedRestrictionRho K t at M is invertible. For a localized supported integral model, apply hR to its integral path model, then supported_coefficient_localization to its root extension. Naturality under the supplied derived isomorphism transports invertibility to M.

The closed-restriction derived-operations theorem makes the two derived section functors triangulated and gives the actual restriction as the three components of a morphism of distinguished triangles. The Mathlib triangle theorem therefore makes P closed under extensions. Induct on extensionProductIter, starting with the localized generators from the preceding step, and apply the finite presentation from the first step. This proves the original rational conclusion with its original signature; ht is retained and unused in this conditional implication.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-945f3f1c0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: unchanged statement, a new 7-step proof, no new nodes, no cycle, every proof step at most 2000 characters, no SGA cited. The math is correct. Step 1: a finitely presented K-module is finite-dimensional, so L is locally K^n (finite-free clause of the presentation-extension node), hence lisse and constructible on qcqs vertices. Step 2: the lattice node's finite-extension case (F=E), then the 'Moreover' refinement clause applied to the one-vertex tree, gives qcqs leaves with actual maps to the strata, lisse O_E-lattices B_W, and closed edges with qc complement, so appended chains stay admissible. Step 3: E_V is flat over O_{E,V} on every vertex (qlbar-colimit node), so the reconstruction node's scalar comparison applies; slice and closed-projection formulas handle the original edges; B_R(t) then applies to H_W. Step 4: flatness gives K-injective preservation (comap node), so one K-K-injective resolution computes both section functors (scalar-coherence clause), and Res(t_K^*I)=t_R^*Res I. Step 5: the ℓ-telescope plus HRS 5.3(1)-style bounded-below continuity on qcqs T and T_0 (det-pe node). BS 6.8.2(2) and HRS 5.3(1) were checked in the PDFs. Step 6: a correct horseshoe 2-of-3 argument. Step 7: induction over the open-closed sequences of the tree. Small cases checked: t=id, T_0 empty, rank 0. The target is not weakened; the torsion hypothesis is kept. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding is a Mathlib leaf (Stacks 01P9 quasi-affine embedding), a generic scheme fact outside the trace formula and Poincaré duality and their proofs, so it is accepted. The 12 declared tool uses are accepted as generic.
